news.context: NRRS Town Fair Tire Cup Series · Round 22 · Talladega
news.title: Talladega Leaves Bell Frustrated as Championship Gap Grows
news.summary: Bell wins Stage 1, leads the most laps and finishes fourth, but leaves one of her strongest tracks two points farther behind in the NRRS championship.
news.cardSummary: Bell wins Stage 1, leads the most laps and finishes fourth, but leaves one of her strongest tracks two points farther behind in the NRRS championship.
news.embedDescription: Bell wins Stage 1, leads the most laps and finishes fourth, but leaves one of her strongest tracks two points farther behind in the NRRS championship.

sections.heading: One Point Closer
paragraphs: TALLADEGA — Hailey Bell came to Talladega with a simple goal.
She did not expect to erase a 65-point championship deficit in one night. She did not even need a dramatic swing.
She just wanted to leave one point closer.
Instead, after spending nearly the entire race at the front of the field, Bell left NRRS Round 22 two points farther behind.

Bell finished fourth in the Palmetto Gaming No. 32 Toyota in the third race of the Chase after starting from the outside of the front row. She won Stage 1, finished third in Stage 2 and led more laps than any other driver.
For most of the race, Bell never ran outside the top three.
Then a late incident reshuffled the running order, and when the race was over, the number Bell cared about most had once again moved in the wrong direction.
She entered Talladega 65 points behind the championship leader. She leaves 67 points back after the championship leader finished second.

sections.heading: A Strong Race, Almost No Movement
paragraphs: “Losing two points is better than losing 20, but Talladega was the race where I wanted to finally gain something,” Bell said. “I didn’t need some huge swing. I just wanted to leave one point closer. I can point to stage finishes and laps led, but none of that changes the standings. I came here needing to gain ground, and I didn’t.”
That made an otherwise strong Talladega performance difficult for Bell to appreciate.
Superspeedway racing has traditionally been one of her strongest disciplines, making Talladega one of the most realistic opportunities remaining for Bell to make progress in the championship.
Instead, one of her strongest races of the Chase produced almost no movement at all.
Matty won the race, followed by the championship leader in second and Outlaw in third. Bell completed the top four.

sections.heading: Trying to Prove She Belongs
paragraphs: For Bell, however, the frustration stretches beyond one race or one finishing position.

A Chase points adjustment previously restored Bell to a position where the championship was again within reach. Since then, she has wanted more than simply to appear in the standings. She has wanted to prove through her own performances that she belongs in the fight.

“I really want to be here,” Bell said. “I want to feel like I matter and like I belong racing with these guys. I want to prove that I’m good enough to be here. But it’s hard to feel that way when every race it feels like I’m digging the hole deeper because I can’t make up the points I need.”
Bell’s frustration is also tied to a pattern that has followed her across multiple series.

She has qualified for every Chase or playoff she has attempted, aided in large part by one of her greatest strengths: consistently showing up. While other competitors have lost significant ground by missing races entirely, Bell has rarely surrendered points through absence.
But once the postseason begins, Bell feels that consistency alone stops being enough.

“I’ve made every Chase or playoff because I show up every week,” Bell said. “Other people miss races and get nothing, while I’m there collecting points. But then we actually get into the championship fight, and I’m usually sitting at or near the bottom because everybody else starts gaining a bunch of points every race and I’m getting close to the minimum.”
For Bell, that has created a difficult distinction between qualifying for a championship fight and feeling competitive once she gets there.

During the regular season, simply being present every week can provide enough consistency to remain in contention. In the Chase, however, Bell feels she has repeatedly struggled to turn that consistency into the finishes necessary to keep pace with the drivers around her.

“I don’t want making the Chase to only mean that I attended more races than somebody else,” Bell said. “I want to get there and actually prove that I deserve to be fighting for something. When everybody else is gaining points and I’m running near the back getting the minimum, it makes it really hard for me to feel like I’m making any progress.”

That cycle has become one of the biggest sources of Bell’s frustration with full-time competition. Showing up has consistently put her in position to compete for championships, but once those championship fights begin, she has struggled to find the performance necessary to turn qualification into contention.
Talladega was painful precisely because it appeared to offer an opportunity to break that pattern.
Instead, even after spending most of the night near the front, Bell left the race two points farther from the championship lead.
That struggle has also affected something Bell wanted to prioritize as the season progressed: enjoying racing again.
For most of Talladega, she did.
Then the championship standings came back into focus.

“I came into tonight wanting to have fun, and for most of the race I did,” Bell said. “But it’s hard to have fun when I’m trying to be good at something and I keep watching the gap go the wrong way. I can have a good race, but if I’m not actually gaining anything, it’s difficult for me to feel good about it.”

sections.heading: Searching for More
paragraphs: Bell has also been candid about another source of frustration: the feeling that attempts to improve at other track types have not produced the progress she wants.

“The hardest part is feeling like every time I try to find more speed, I lose something somewhere else,” Bell said. “I want to feel like I belong here and that I’m contributing, but right now I’m struggling to see that in the results.”

sections.heading: A Different Team Environment Ahead
paragraphs: Next season will at least bring a different team environment, with Bell expecting to have more teammates around her on track.
She is not treating that as an automatic solution.

“I’m looking forward to actually having teammates next season, because right now there are a lot of races where I feel like I’m on my own,” Bell said. “But I also know that having teammates isn’t suddenly going to fix everything for me. If they’re running at the front and I’m in the back, there’s not much they can do for me anyway. I still have to find a way to put myself in position first, and that’s the part I’ve been struggling with.”

For Bell, that makes the hope of having teammates less about expecting someone else to rescue her races and more about wanting the opportunity to finally be part of a group when she is in position to contribute.
But after another night where a strong performance failed to translate into meaningful championship progress, even that future possibility feels difficult for Bell to lean on as reassurance.

sections.heading: Why 2027 Will Be the Final Full-Time Season
paragraphs: That frustration has also become part of Bell’s reasoning for making 2027 her final season of full-time competition.

Bell has grown increasingly discouraged by a competitive landscape in which the same small group of drivers continues to control much of the winning, while her own efforts have struggled to translate into meaningful progress. Although she plans to remain involved in racing, the pressure and commitment of competing full-time has become harder to justify when the experience itself has become increasingly difficult to enjoy.

“The biggest reason I’m stepping away from full-time competition after next season is that I’m tired of watching the same people win every week while feeling like I can’t make any progress,” Bell said. “I want racing to be something I enjoy again. Right now, it doesn’t feel that way.”

For Bell, next season is not being treated as a farewell from racing entirely. Instead, it will mark the end of her commitment to full-time competition, with the hope that stepping away from chasing every race and every point will eventually allow racing to feel enjoyable again.

sections.heading: Three Races Remain
paragraphs: Three races remain in the NRRS season: Portland, New Hampshire and Homestead.

The upcoming schedule makes Talladega particularly difficult to leave behind. Portland and New Hampshire represent two of Bell’s weaker track types from a performance standpoint, leaving one of her strongest opportunities for a championship gain behind her without the progress she hoped to make.
On paper, Talladega was one of Bell’s strongest races of the Chase.
She started second. She won a stage. She finished inside the top three in both stages. She led the most laps. She finished fourth.
But those were not the numbers Bell was looking at afterward.
She was looking at 67.
“I wanted to prove something tonight,” Bell said. “I wanted to leave knowing I had actually made progress. I didn’t. That’s what hurts.”
With three races remaining, Bell leaves Talladega less concerned with finding positives in a strong performance than with one question that has followed her throughout the Chase:
How can a driver run near the front all night and still feel no closer to where she is trying to go?

news.context: 2027 FULL HEART Tour · Final Full-Time Season
news.title: Hailey Bell Announces 2027 “Full Heart” Tour, Final Full-Time Season
news.summary: Hailey Bell has announced that the 2027 season will be her final year competing full-time, bringing one chapter of her racing career to a close with a season-long celebration known as the FULL HEART Tour. The tour will celebrate the people, partners, cars, moments and memories that shaped Bell’s racing career while she competes one final season on a full-time schedule.

quote.text: This isn’t really about saying goodbye. It’s about getting one more opportunity to celebrate everything that got me here — the people I’ve raced with, the friends I’ve made, the sponsors that became part of my identity and everybody who supported me along the way. I want this last full-time season to feel like it comes from the heart and honors the whole story.

timeline.title: Where the Full-Time Story Began
timeline.method: Bell’s first full-time NSS campaign featured Toys “R” Us, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen and Apex Sim Racing — three partners that will return for FULL HEART.

timeline.title: The Identity Built Along the Way
timeline.method: PetSmart, Mobil 1, Rheem, Home Depot, Ghost Energy and Ironmouse represent the modern chapter of Bell’s racing identity heading into 2027.

timeline.title: One More Full-Time Season
timeline.method: Past and present meet through special paint schemes, returning partners, throwbacks and tributes while Bell continues to race for wins and championships.

timeline.title: A Career Told Through Paint
timeline.method: Selected events become individual chapters built around sponsors, seasons, memories, milestones, teammates, friends and defining moments from Bell’s career.

timeline.title: Full-Time Ends, Racing Does Not Have To
timeline.method: The end of the 2027 season closes Bell’s weekly full-season commitments, while one-off appearances, special events and part-time starts remain possible.

sections.heading: Full Heart
paragraphs: Rather than treating 2027 simply as a farewell, Bell wants the season to connect where her full-time career began with where it will ultimately end.

The name FULL HEART represents the passion, gratitude and emotion Bell wants the 2027 season to carry. Past and present will meet throughout the year through special paint schemes, returning partners, throwbacks and tributes to important moments throughout her career.

Current partners including PetSmart, Mobil 1, Rheem, Home Depot, Ghost Energy and Ironmouse will help represent Bell’s modern racing identity. But FULL HEART will also reach all the way back to the beginning of her full-time career.

sections.heading: Where It Began
paragraphs: Bell’s first full-time NSS campaign came in Season 3.
Three partners associated with that first full-time season will return in 2027: Toys “R” Us, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen and Apex Sim Racing.
Their return creates one of the central themes of FULL HEART. The same brands that were part of Bell’s first season as a full-time competitor will return during her final one.

Each will receive special appearances during 2027 celebrating Bell’s early racing years and the journey from her first full-time season to her last. The returning partnerships are intended to feel authentic to their original eras, with paint schemes and promotional material drawing inspiration from the cars and visual identity associated with Bell’s Season 3 campaign.
From the first full-time season to the final one — with gratitude for every step in between. That is FULL HEART.

sections.heading: More Than a Farewell
paragraphs: Bell’s decision applies specifically to full-time competition. After the conclusion of the 2027 season, Bell will step back from full-time competition and end her weekly, full-season racing commitments, but it does not necessarily mean the final race of her career.
Future one-off appearances, special events or part-time starts remain possible. For Bell, that distinction is important.

Racing has been too significant a part of her story for the final full-time season to be framed entirely around an ending. FULL HEART is instead intended as a celebration of everything that came before while leaving the door open for whatever may come afterward.

“I still want 2027 to be about racing,” Bell said. “I don’t want every weekend to feel like everybody is waiting for the last lap. I still want to win races. I still want to fight for championships. I still want to have fun with my friends. We’re just going to celebrate a lot of memories while we do it.”

sections.heading: One More Shot
paragraphs: The FULL HEART Tour will not be a ceremonial season. Bell intends to approach 2027 with the same competitive goals as any other year.
Every race still counts. Every win still matters. And if a championship opportunity presents itself, Bell intends to chase it.

What changes is everything surrounding those races. Throughout the season, selected events will feature commemorative paint schemes, returning sponsors, historical references and tributes highlighting different chapters of Bell’s racing career.
Some cars will recreate familiar ideas from the past. Others will reinterpret those designs through Bell’s current identity. Several will bring pieces of multiple eras together on one car.

sections.heading: A Career Told Through Paint
paragraphs: Paint schemes have always been one of the most recognizable parts of Bell’s racing identity, making them a major component of FULL HEART.
PetSmart will remain one of the defining brands of Bell’s modern era. Mobil 1, Rheem, Home Depot, Ghost Energy and Ironmouse will also play roles throughout the final full-time campaign.
Then come the cars representing where the journey began. Toys “R” Us, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen and Apex Sim Racing will each return as direct callbacks to Bell’s first full-time NSS season.
Those appearances will not simply place old logos on modern cars. Each design will be treated as another chapter in the FULL HEART story.

Throughout 2027, additional cars may celebrate important races, previous designs, career milestones, teammates, friends and memorable moments from Bell’s history. Together, the cars will tell the story of her career one race at a time.

sections.heading: Every Chapter
paragraphs: Special FULL HEART schemes throughout 2027 will be presented as individual chapters of Bell’s career. Each chapter may highlight a different sponsor, season, memory, milestone or era.
FULL HEART // CHAPTER 01 — a look back at an early career moment.
FULL HEART // CHAPTER 02 — a returning partner or historic paint scheme.
FULL HEART // CHAPTER 03 — a championship, memorable race or important career milestone.

The chapter system will continue throughout the season, eventually building a visual timeline of Bell’s full-time career. By the end of 2027, the complete FULL HEART collection will serve as a permanent record of the journey.

sections.heading: Thank You for the Ride
paragraphs: While FULL HEART tells Bell’s story, the season is equally intended as a thank-you to everyone who became part of it — teammates, competitors, friends, league organizers, designers, partners, fans and everyone who spent a race night in voice chat, watched a finish unfold, worked on a car, celebrated a win or simply stayed along for the ride.
Those relationships are ultimately what Bell wants remembered most.

“Trophies and wins are awesome, but when I think about racing, I think about the people,” Bell said. “Some of my favorite memories aren’t even things that would show up on a stat sheet. They’re the nights we were all together having fun. That’s what made all of this worth doing.”

sections.heading: From Season 3 to 2027
paragraphs: Years before FULL HEART, Bell entered her first full-time NSS season in Season 3.
Toys “R” Us was there. Cheddar’s was there. Apex Sim Racing was there.
In 2027, they will be there again.
Different cars. Different years. A different Hailey. But part of the same story.

That connection between Bell’s first and final full-time campaigns is what gives the tour its heart. It is a season built around gratitude, passion and the people who shaped Bell’s career. Full heart.

sections.heading: The Final Full-Time Lap
paragraphs: There will eventually be a final starting grid. A final full-time green flag. A final championship chase.
And somewhere during the closing race of 2027, Bell will begin the final lap of her career as a full-time competitor.
Until then, there is another season to run. More races to win. More memories to make. And a few old friends coming back along the way.
Hailey Bell’s FULL HEART Tour begins in 2027.

news.title: North Wilkesboro Reshapes the NRRS Chase Picture
news.summary: Trent won Race 21 at North Wilkesboro, while Will moved to the championship lead. Hailey remains sixth in the Chase with 2,087 points, 108 behind the leader.

sections.heading: Race 21 at North Wilkesboro
paragraphs: Trent won the second race of the NRRS Chase at North Wilkesboro Speedway. The corrected race payout credited Trent with 58 points, including eight Stage 1 points and 10 Stage 2 points.
Jaxon finished second, followed by Clutch, Outlaw, Will, Max Verstappen, and Matty among the confirmed finishers in the published result.

sections.heading: The Chase After Race 21
paragraphs: Will leaves North Wilkesboro as the championship leader with 2,195 points. Trent is second with 2,182, followed by Clutch at 2,173, Jaxon at 2,130, and Outlaw at 2,128.

Hailey remains sixth with 2,087 points, 108 behind the leader. The updated board replaces the earlier 110-point display and keeps the public championship panel aligned with the corrected Race 21 standings.

sections.heading: One Source of Truth
paragraphs: Aetherwing now treats the published race result as the source for Latest Result and can advance standings boards automatically when Auto Points is enabled. That reduces the need to enter the same race data again in a separate standings editor.

news.context: NRRS Town Fair Tire Cup Series
news.title: Hailey Fights Back to Top Five in Southern 500 Chase Opener
news.summary: A P9 start, a difficult night without stage points, and a recovery through the pit cycle ended with Hailey bringing the #32 Aetherwing entry home fifth at Darlington. The finish offered something meaningful to build on even as the Chase points picture remained challenging.

quote.text: Had hopes, but it wasn't the night I needed. I missed out on stage points again, but fought back from the pit cycle and finished Top 5. It's frustrating when the effort isn't matching what I envision, but I still consider this a big success for me. I made the Chase, and all I can do is keep racing, keep trying to improve, and hope we can put together a few really good runs.

sections.heading: A Top Five That Meant More
paragraphs: The Southern 500 did not unfold the way Hailey hoped when the NRRS Chase opened at Darlington, but the final result still carried real weight. Starting ninth in the #32 Aetherwing entry, Hailey went through another race without collecting stage points before working back through the pit cycle and finishing fifth.

On paper, P5 is a strong way to begin a five-race championship run. For Hailey, the significance was more personal. Recent races have often felt like a fight to turn effort into sustainable pace, making a top-five recovery at one of the schedule's most demanding tracks a result worth recognizing rather than dismissing.

sections.heading: The Stage-Point Problem
paragraphs: The frustration came from where the points were not scored. With zero stage points at Darlington, the #32 was forced to rely entirely on the finishing result while other Chase contenders had opportunities to add points earlier in the race.

Hailey has been open about how difficult that pattern has become. Completing a pass does not always mean being able to keep the position; when stronger exit speed brings the same car immediately back to the rear bumper, prolonged battles can turn into mistakes or force a decision to give the position back and protect the overall race. That makes stage-point opportunities especially difficult to capitalize on.

sections.heading: Frustrated, Not Finished
paragraphs: The result did not erase the larger concerns. Hailey left Darlington sixth in the Chase standings with 2,087 points, 58 behind the championship leader and one position lower than entering the race. The gap reinforces how difficult moving forward could become without finding stage points and additional pace.

But the outlook is not resignation. Hailey remains grateful for the opportunity to have made the Chase and for the success already earned, while being realistic about how much work remains. That combination of ambition, frustration, gratitude, and persistence is why the Darlington fifth-place finish was viewed inside the #32 camp as a genuine success.

sections.heading: Keep Racing
paragraphs: Darlington was the first of five Chase races, not the final verdict on the season. The remaining schedule sends NRRS to Richmond, Kansas, the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Road Course, New Hampshire, and Homestead-Miami for the championship finale.

The immediate task is simple even if the solution is not: keep racing, keep looking for opportunities to improve the car's position throughout the night, and try to turn a few strong finishes into complete races. The Verizon 400 at Richmond on September 22 is the next chance to do exactly that.

callout.label: Driver Perspective
callout.title: Frustrated, Still Fighting
callout.text: The P5 finish did not solve the stage-point problem, but it gave the #32 team a meaningful result to carry forward. The goal now is to build complete races around that same fight-back speed.

news.title: Hailey Bell Joins StarClutch Racing for NRRS Season 4
news.summary: StarClutch Racing owner Clutch announced on September 14 that Hailey Bell will drive the #28 for SCR in NRRS Season 4, bringing PetSmart sponsorship with her. Aetherwing team partner Palmetto Gaming will also appear on Bell’s #28 at SCR, while Aetherwing plans to continue its own NRRS program with the #32, #42 and #46.

sections.heading: The #28 Heads to StarClutch Racing
paragraphs: StarClutch Racing owner Clutch announced on September 14 that Hailey Bell will join the organization as one of its drivers for Season 4 of NRRS.

Bell will take the #28 with her to SCR. PetSmart will remain attached to the program as a sponsor, giving the Season 4 entry a direct continuation of one of Bell’s most recognizable personal partnerships.

sections.heading: Palmetto Gaming Remains an Aetherwing Partner
paragraphs: Palmetto Gaming remains an Aetherwing eMotorsports team partner and will also be part of Hailey Bell’s #28 program at StarClutch Racing next season.
Its presence on Bell’s SCR car does not change the broader team partnership with Aetherwing. Bell will race the #28 for SCR while Aetherwing continues to operate its own NRRS program separately.

sections.heading: Aetherwing Is Staying in NRRS
paragraphs: Aetherwing’s planned NRRS charter lineup for Season 4 is #32, #42 and #46. The team is not leaving the series when Bell moves to the SCR #28.

Instead, the Season 4 structure expands the relationship between Aetherwing and StarClutch Racing: Bell competes full-time for SCR while Aetherwing continues with its own cars, drivers and long-term program.

callout.label: Season 4 Structure
callout.title: #28 at SCR. #32 / #42 / #46 at Aetherwing.
callout.text: Hailey Bell will take the #28 and PetSmart sponsorship to StarClutch Racing for NRRS Season 4. Aetherwing team partner Palmetto Gaming will also appear on Bell’s #28 at SCR, while Aetherwing continues in NRRS with the #32, #42 and #46 as a separate team program.

programBreakdown.title: Planned NRRS Charters
items: Separate team program from Hailey’s SCR #28

news.title: Hailey Clinches Third Straight NRRS Chase Berth at Martinsville
news.summary: A P4 finish in the Goody's Fast Relief 500 officially locked Hailey and the #32 Aetherwing entry into the NRRS Season 3 Chase, marking a third consecutive NRRS postseason appearance and fifth confirmed Chase qualification overall.

sections.heading: Locked In at Martinsville
paragraphs: Martinsville delivered more than another strong finish for Hailey. Bringing the #32 Aetherwing entry home fourth in the Goody's Fast Relief 500 mathematically secured a place in the NRRS Season 3 Chase and extended one of the most consistent postseason runs in Hailey's recorded RoRacing career.

Hailey started seventh and finished fourth for 33 finishing points. A fifth-place Stage 2 result added six points after an eighth-place Stage 1, producing 39 race points for the night. The result left Hailey sixth in the standings with 553 points, 196 behind the championship leader and 211 points above the Chase cutoff.

sections.heading: Three Straight in NRRS
paragraphs: The Martinsville clinch continued a streak that began in NRRS Season 1. Hailey has now qualified for the Chase in each of the first three recorded NRRS postseason campaigns: Season 1 on points, Season 2 through an All-Star victory, and Season 3 on points after Martinsville.

The routes were different each time. Regular-season consistency carried the first berth, the Season 2 Miami All-Star victory provided a direct win-in, and the Season 3 #32 built enough of a points cushion to secure the spot before the regular season was finished.

sections.heading: Five Berths, Three Series
paragraphs: NRRS accounts for three of the five confirmed Chase appearances, but the postseason résumé extends beyond one league. A Kmart Season 1 berth was earned on points after Kansas, while the UARL Season 4 regular-season finale at Indianapolis produced a race-winning ticket into that championship field.

The record now stands at three NRRS berths, one Kmart berth, and one UARL berth. Two of those five were secured directly through victories: the NRRS Season 2 All-Star Race at Miami and the UARL Season 4 finale at Indianapolis.

sections.heading: The Championship Fight Is Next
paragraphs: Martinsville did not finish the job; it guaranteed the opportunity to keep fighting for it. With the Season 3 Chase berth secure, Hailey and the #32 program could turn fully toward the postseason and another chance to convert a Chase appearance into a championship run.

Whatever came next, the qualification itself added another permanent marker to the record book: five confirmed Chase appearances across three series and three consecutive seasons in the NRRS championship field.

callout.label: Postseason Résumé
callout.title: Five Trips Into The Fight
callout.text: NRRS ×3 · Kmart ×1 · UARL ×1. Two of the five confirmed berths were secured through race victories.

news.title: Hailey Finishes 2nd in Historic 100th RoRacing Start
news.summary: Hailey marked her 100th career RoRacing start with a Stage 1 win and runner-up finish at Talladega, scoring 50 points and moving up one spot to fourth in the NRRS standings after avoiding multiple wrecks and rebounding from setbacks.

sections.heading: Start Number 100
paragraphs: Talladega became the setting for a major career marker as Hailey made the 100th recorded RoRacing start. The milestone race became more than a ceremonial number: the #32 program left the event with a stage victory, a runner-up finish, and a meaningful points haul.
The result came after a race that required recovery as much as outright speed. Hailey avoided multiple incidents and rebounded from setbacks instead of letting the milestone race unravel.

sections.heading: Stage Win, Then a Runner-Up Finish
paragraphs: A Stage 1 victory put the milestone on the board early. By the checkered flag, Hailey had converted the day into a second-place finish at Talladega and 50 total points.
That combination made the 100th start one of the stronger all-around results in the recorded career: a stage win, a podium-level finish, and points that mattered to the championship picture.

sections.heading: A Milestone That Moved the Standings
paragraphs: The Talladega result moved Hailey up one position to fourth in the NRRS standings. Instead of the 100th start living only as a career-count statistic, it directly improved the competitive position of the #32 team.
The story was preserved in the Team Wire because it combined the personal milestone with an actual race-day result — exactly the kind of moment the archive was built to keep.

callout.label: Milestone File
callout.title: 100 Starts · 50 Points
callout.text: Stage 1 win, runner-up finish, and a move to fourth in the NRRS standings in Hailey's 100th recorded RoRacing start.

news.title: Waggoner Sweeps Michigan Double
news.summary: Nicholas Waggoner followed up his NASCAR iRacing Series Michigan win by capturing the NASCAR Class C Series - Fixed truck race, completing a two-win Michigan weekend and giving Aetherwing its 25th recorded race victory.

sections.heading: Two Wins in One Michigan Weekend
paragraphs: Nicholas Waggoner completed a Michigan sweep by following the June 5 NASCAR iRacing Series victory with a June 7 win in the NASCAR Class C Series - Fixed truck race.
The second checkered flag turned an already significant weekend into a two-win run across two different iRacing NASCAR disciplines at the same track.

sections.heading: The Truck Win Marked Number 25
paragraphs: The Class C Series - Fixed victory also carried an organizational milestone: it became Aetherwing's 25th recorded team win in the modern record book.
That placed the Michigan truck result in two parts of the archive at once — as the completion of Waggoner's Michigan double and as the victory that pushed the team-win count to 25.

sections.heading: From Photo Finish to Weekend Sweep
paragraphs: Just two days earlier, Waggoner had won the NASCAR iRacing Series race at Michigan by 0.029 seconds. The truck victory meant the photo-finish breakthrough was not an isolated result; it became the first half of a complete Michigan double.
The back-to-back Michigan victories remain grouped in the record book as one of the defining iRacing weekends of the Aetherwing era.

callout.label: Record Book
callout.title: Victory No. 25
callout.text: The June 7 Michigan truck win completed a two-race weekend sweep and became Aetherwing's 25th recorded team victory.

news.title: Waggoner Wins Michigan NIS Thriller for Rowdy
news.summary: Nicholas Waggoner scored an emotional NASCAR iRacing Series victory at Michigan in a photo finish, winning by 0.029 seconds in the #28 Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen Toyota and dedicating the win to Kyle “Rowdy” Busch.

sections.heading: A Michigan Win Decided at the Line
paragraphs: Nicholas Waggoner put the #28 Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen Toyota into Victory Lane in the NASCAR iRacing Series at Michigan, with the result decided by only 0.029 seconds.
The margin made the victory a true photo finish and immediately gave the race a permanent place in the Aetherwing record book.

sections.heading: For Rowdy
paragraphs: The result carried an emotional layer beyond the finishing margin. Waggoner dedicated the Michigan victory to Kyle “Rowdy” Busch, making the race one of the more personal wins preserved in the team's iRacing history.
The combination of the #28 entry, Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen livery, razor-thin margin, and dedication is why the Team Wire keeps the event as more than a line in the win table.

sections.heading: The First Half of a Michigan Double
paragraphs: The NIS win became the opening act of an even bigger weekend. Two days later, Waggoner won the NASCAR Class C Series - Fixed truck race at Michigan as well.
Together, the June 5 and June 7 victories formed a two-win Michigan sweep, with the second result becoming Aetherwing's 25th recorded team win.

callout.label: Finish Margin
callout.title: 0.029 Seconds
callout.text: The #28 Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen Toyota won the NASCAR iRacing Series race at Michigan in a photo finish.

news.title: Waggoner Wins the Indianapolis 500 on iRacing
news.summary: Nicholas Waggoner delivered a crown-jewel victory for Aetherwing, winning the Indianapolis 500 on iRacing and adding one of sim racing’s biggest oval trophies to the team record book.

sections.heading: A Crown Jewel Goes Into the Record Book
paragraphs: Nicholas Waggoner won the Indianapolis 500 on iRacing on May 15, 2026, delivering one of the biggest oval victories in Aetherwing's recorded sim-racing history.
The result was preserved as a crown-jewel win rather than an ordinary race victory because of the event's place in the iRacing program and the wider motorsports calendar.

sections.heading: First iRacing Crown Jewel for Aetherwing
paragraphs: The Indianapolis victory became Aetherwing's first recorded iRacing crown-jewel win. That distinction placed it alongside the team's other major firsts and milestones in Wins & History.
For the Factory Program, the result gave the organization a marquee event victory to anchor the 2026 iRacing season.

sections.heading: Part of a Breakout Run
paragraphs: The Indianapolis 500 win came less than a month before Waggoner's two-win Michigan weekend. By early June, the record book showed Indianapolis, the Michigan NASCAR iRacing Series race, and the Michigan truck race in quick succession.
That run made the Indianapolis 500 not only a standalone crown jewel, but the beginning of one of the strongest stretches in the team's recorded iRacing history.

callout.label: Milestone
callout.title: First iRacing Crown Jewel
callout.text: The May 15 Indianapolis 500 victory is recorded as Aetherwing's first iRacing crown-jewel win.

news.title: Aetherwing Sweeps the Clashes
news.summary: Aetherwing opened the 2026 RoRacing season with a two-league statement as Jaxon won the NRRS Clash and Jayden completed the sweep with a UARL Clash victory.

sections.heading: Jaxon Strikes First in NRRS
paragraphs: The new RoRacing season opened with Jaxon putting Aetherwing in Victory Lane in the NRRS Clash at Target Speedway. The preseason exhibition demanded clean execution through aggressive racing, and Jaxon stayed positioned for the move that mattered.
The win gave the organization an immediate statement result before championship points even began.

sections.heading: Jayden Completes the Sweep in UARL
paragraphs: Season 4 D1 champion Jayden carried that momentum into the UARL Clash and delivered the second win of the opening stretch.
With one victory in each league's preseason showcase, Aetherwing turned the start of the season into an organizational sweep rather than a single isolated result.

sections.heading: Setting the Standard for the Regular Season
paragraphs: The two Clash wins gave the team early evidence of competitive pace and coordination across both programs. The original story framed the weekend as a tone-setter for the regular season and the championship campaigns ahead.
The article also captured the team identity of that moment, including the GR Aetherwing presentation and the roster that represented the organization during that historical period.

quote.text: Winning a Clash event is about more than just grabbing a trophy—it’s about establishing dominance before the championship points even start counting.

callout.label: Opening Statement
callout.title: Two Clashes · Two Wins
callout.text: Jaxon won the NRRS Clash at Target Speedway and Jayden completed the sweep with a UARL Clash victory.

news.title: Aetherwing and NGM Build Driver Development Pathway
news.summary: Aetherwing partnered with Nico Goated Motorsports, the team owned by Nico, to create a development pathway for future NRRS and Kmart Cup talent.

sections.heading: A Clearer Road Into Aetherwing
paragraphs: Aetherwing announced a strategic partnership with Nico Goated Motorsports, the team owned by Nico, to support the Driver Development Program and create a more deliberate entry point for new talent.
Instead of moving every prospect directly into the primary roster, the development structure was designed to scout, evaluate, and prepare drivers before larger opportunities were considered.

sections.heading: Development Through Competition
paragraphs: The program centered its competitive pathway on environments connected to NRRS and Kmart Cup Series racing. Speed mattered, but the evaluation was intentionally broader than lap time alone.

Consistency, availability, attitude, race craft, preparation, communication, and long-term commitment were all part of the development focus. Successful participants could be considered for reserve or primary-roster opportunities.

sections.heading: Scout · Develop · Promote
paragraphs: The pathway was organized around three steps. Scout meant identifying new drivers, watching race craft, and tracking availability. Develop meant building consistency, improving communication, and learning team standards. Promote meant opening reserve or primary opportunities for drivers who proved they fit the long-term organization.
The structure gave Aetherwing a middle step between outside competition and direct signing, while NGM provided a development partner familiar with the RoRacing environment.

sections.heading: Why It Mattered
paragraphs: The partnership gave Aetherwing a more structured approach to roster growth and established a repeatable talent pipeline instead of relying only on immediate signings.
The original program announcement positioned the NGM relationship as a foundation for future growth across the team's NRRS and Kmart Cup efforts.

quote.text: This is about building the next wave — not just finding fast drivers, but finding the right drivers.

callout.label: Evaluation Focus
callout.title: Consistency · Availability · Attitude
callout.text: Race craft, preparation, communication and long-term team fit were part of the development review alongside outright speed.

news.title: BellSouth Becomes Aetherwing
news.summary: BellSouth eMotorsports officially became Aetherwing eMotorsports, launching a sharper identity built for NR2003, Roblox RoRacing, iRacing, and the future of the team.

sections.heading: A New Identity
paragraphs: After building the modern foundation under the BellSouth eMotorsports name, the organization officially launched its next chapter as Aetherwing eMotorsports.

The change was presented as more than a new name. Aetherwing represented a more original long-term identity, a stronger presentation system, and a competitive direction designed to work across NR2003, Roblox RoRacing, and iRacing.

sections.heading: What BellSouth Built
paragraphs: The BellSouth era carried the team into its modern sim-racing phase, especially after entering NR2003 competition in late 2023. Expansion into Roblox RoRacing and iRacing followed in 2024, creating the foundation for a larger multi-program organization.

That history was not discarded by the rebrand. The Aetherwing identity was designed to carry the record and organizational lineage forward while giving the modern team a brand that could stand on its own.

sections.heading: Built to Grow Beyond One Program
paragraphs: The launch introduced a more aggressive visual direction and a clearer competitive structure. The 2026 identity was built to support a growing roster, partner network, record book, and development path rather than being tied to one league or platform.
The rebrand created a clean starting point for the next phase without rewriting the BellSouth chapter that led to it.

sections.heading: The Timeline Into Aetherwing
paragraphs: The organizational lineage begins with Silph Co. Motorsports in the NASCAR 15 era, returns as BellSouth Racing during the NASCAR Heat era, enters NR2003 as BellSouth eMotorsports in 2023, expands into RoRacing and iRacing in 2024, and becomes Aetherwing eMotorsports in 2026.
That sequence remains part of the public history because the Aetherwing era is a continuation of the same organization rather than a replacement history.

quote.text: Born to soar. Built to fight.

callout.label: Identity File
callout.title: BellSouth → Aetherwing
callout.text: A new name and visual direction carried the existing modern team history forward into the 2026 Aetherwing era.

news.title: Hailey Scores First RoRacing Win
news.summary: Hailey broke through in the NRRS Season 2 All-Star Race, taking the #28 Aetherwing entry to Victory Lane for her first career RoRacing win.

sections.heading: Hailey Is Officially a Race Winner
paragraphs: The NRRS Season 2 All-Star Race became the breakthrough night for Hailey, as the #28 Aetherwing entry survived a chaotic non-points showcase and reached Victory Lane for the first recorded RoRacing win of the career.
The All-Star format brought segment breaks, resets, and repeated opportunities for strategy to change the running order, making execution as important as raw pace.

sections.heading: The Final Stage
paragraphs: Hailey and the team kept the opening portions controlled, prioritizing track position and clean exits before committing to a more aggressive plan for the final stage. A well-timed stop and strong restart pace put the #28 inside the top three as the race moved toward its finish.

On the final run, Hailey cleared traffic, defended the high lane, and controlled the race while the battle behind developed. The late pressure was not enough to take the lead away, and the #28 crossed the line first.

sections.heading: A Breakthrough Beyond the Points
paragraphs: The All-Star Race did not award championship points, but the significance of the result was much bigger than the scoring format. It was the first proof in the record book that Hailey could turn the pace, racecraft, and strategy into a race victory.
The win later became even more important to the postseason story: the Season 2 All-Star victory also secured Hailey's second NRRS Chase berth.

callout.label: Career First
callout.title: Victory Lane · Dec 2, 2025
callout.text: The #28 Aetherwing entry won the NRRS Season 2 All-Star Race for Hailey's first recorded career RoRacing victory.

news.title: Aetherwing Scores 1-2 in Kmart Cup Daytona 500
news.summary: Flamingo won the Kmart Cup Series Season 1 Daytona 500 with teammate Will pushing him to the line, giving Aetherwing its first points-paying victory and a historic 1-2 finish.

sections.heading: A Landmark Daytona 500 Win
paragraphs: The 2025–26 Kmart Cup Series opened with Flamingo taking the #22 Apex Sim Racing Chevrolet to victory in the Daytona 500 on September 22, 2025.
The win became Aetherwing's first points-paying victory and delivered a crown-jewel result at the beginning of the season.

sections.heading: Flamingo and Will Break Away Together
paragraphs: Drafting partnerships shaped the closing laps. Flamingo and teammate Will in the #94 linked together after the final restart, using the two-car push to create separation from the rest of the field.
The coordination turned the race from a fight for one Aetherwing win into a chance to bring both cars home at the front.

sections.heading: The White Flag Protection
paragraphs: On the final lap, Will protected Flamingo's rear quarter while the pair worked through Turns 3 and 4 and defended against a late challenge from behind.
Flamingo reached the checkered flag first and Will finished second, completing the 1–2 sweep in one of the biggest races on the Kmart Cup schedule.

sections.heading: A Season-Opening Statement
paragraphs: The result gave Flamingo a first Daytona 500 victory, put Aetherwing's first crown jewel of the season into the record book, and followed Will's Budweiser Shootout victory one week earlier.
The original race report framed the back-to-back Daytona results as a major early-season momentum swing for the organization.

callout.label: Historic Finish
callout.title: Aetherwing 1–2 at Daytona
callout.text: Flamingo won the Daytona 500 with teammate Will second, delivering the team's first points-paying victory and a crown-jewel sweep of the top two positions.
